findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The PPHQN5 ticket and product plan stay inside the observer-only boundary that the C7HCN7 recovery plan proposes. Certification, closing integration, shared gates, #5857 merge, CKWE2D, paid/live runs and cloud/OpenCode are all excluded in both scope and non-goals. R1–R5 match the plan's observer requirements: no caller-supplied ticket, command, report, filter or success flag; complete required assertions including parameter rows; separate handling of unrelated skips; authenticated records under a distinct purpose; retained failed attempts; freshness that keeps history readable; and no credit for the 33 historical deferrals. The persona (SWM) and surface names match the project registries. I found no concrete release-relevant failure. A few spec items are still loosely defined, and implementation planning should settle them before scenarios or code.

R4 says "legitimate audit-only output writes preserve currency" but never defines "legitimate". The recovery plan asks for a stated projection of ticket.md before implementation: identity, scope, out_of_scope, done_when and parent linkage stay bound, while status, phase, timestamp and Work Log are separate. It also forbids exempting the whole ticket. The spec only says lifecycle outputs are not blanket exemptions. If an implementation treated all of ticket.md as a lifecycle output, a change to accepted scope after observation could still verify as current. That would go against the scope-binding intent of R1 and R4. Write this projection into the Rules or scenarios before implementation planning.

R2 says the fixed mapping covers all 37 delivery cases. The recovery plan says the current proof registrations are only a starting point and that a row which can't be supported should be reported as unsupported. The spec has no outcome for that case other than refusal, so if any case lacks a real assertion, done_when can never be met, or there is pressure to invent an assertion. State that an unsupported case produces a named refusal and must not be filled with a new or weakened assertion.

The spec doesn't say who approves the 'fixed approved proof set' or the case-to-assertion mapping, or where they come from. It also doesn't say how the 'bound clean committed candidate' is chosen (pinned commit, current HEAD, or something else). R4's freshness check limits the damage of a stale candidate, and later certification judges semantic adequacy, so this isn't blocking. Still, 'Unresolved product decisions: None' overstates how settled the binding source is. Record where the approved profile comes from as an implementation-planning obligation.
The ticket's created/last_modified timestamp (2026-10-24T01:32Z) is UTC and is later than the local review date. This is a timezone difference, not a defect.
